# Gospel of Philip — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, pp. 51-86 | Coptic

---

## Chapter 1

**1** A Hebrew [ϩⲉⲃⲣⲁⲓⲟⲥ] makes a Hebrew [ϩⲉⲃⲣⲁⲓⲟⲥ], and such a one is called a proselyte [ⲡⲣⲟⲥⲏⲗⲩⲧⲟⲥ]. But a proselyte does not make a proselyte. [Others] are as they are [ⲛⲉⲧⲙⲙⲁⲩ ⲛⲉ ⲛⲉⲧⲙⲙⲁⲩ] and make others like themselves, while others simply come into being [ϣⲱⲡⲉ].

**2** The slave [ϩⲙϩⲁⲗ] seeks only to be free [ⲣⲙϩⲉ], but does not seek the estate [ⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ] of his master [ⲡⲉϥϫⲟⲉⲓⲥ]. But the son [ϣⲏⲣⲉ] is not only a son but lays claim to the inheritance [ⲕⲗⲏⲣⲟⲛⲟⲙⲓⲁ] of the father [ⲡⲉϥⲉⲓⲱⲧ].

**3** Those who inherit [ⲉⲧⲉⲣⲕⲗⲏⲣⲟⲛⲟⲙⲉⲓ] the dead [ⲉⲧ ⲙⲟⲟⲩⲧ] are themselves dead, and they inherit the dead. Those who inherit the living [ⲉⲧⲟⲛϩ] are themselves alive, and they inherit both the living and the dead.

**4** The dead do not inherit [ⲧⲉⲕⲗⲏⲣⲟⲛⲟⲙⲓⲁ]. For how could a dead person inherit? If the dead one inherits the living, he will not die, but the dead one will live all the more.

**5** A Gentile [ⲉⲑⲛⲓⲕⲟⲥ] does not die, for he has never lived [ⲟⲛϩ] so that he might die. Whoever has believed [ⲡⲓⲥⲧⲉⲩⲉ] the truth [ⲙⲉ] has lived, and this one is in danger of dying — for he is alive.

**6** Since Christ came [ⲁⲩⲱ ⲛⲧⲉⲣⲉⲭⲣⲓⲥⲧⲟⲥ ⲉⲓ], the world [ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ] was created [ⲥⲱⲛⲧ], the cities [ⲡⲟⲗⲓⲥ] were established, the dead were buried [ⲕⲱϩ].

**7** When we were Hebrews we were orphans [ⲟⲣⲫⲁⲛⲟⲥ], with only the mother [ⲙⲁⲁⲩ]. But when we became Christians [ⲭⲣⲓⲥⲧⲓⲁⲛⲟⲥ] we came to have both father [ⲉⲓⲱⲧ] and mother [ⲙⲁⲁⲩ].

**8** Those who sow in winter harvest in summer. The winter [ⲉⲓⲱⲣϩ] is the world [ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ]; the summer [ⲉⲓⲱⲣϩ ⲛϣⲟⲙⲛⲧ] is the other aeon [ⲁⲓⲱⲛ]. Let us sow [ϫⲟ] in the world so that we may harvest in summer. Because of this it is fitting [ⲕⲁⲗⲱⲥ] for us not to pray [ϣⲗⲏⲗ] in winter.

**9** What comes forth [ⲉⲃⲟⲗ ϩⲙ] from winter is summer. But if anyone reaps in winter he will not actually reap but will uproot [ⲛϣ ⲛⲧⲁϩⲉ] since this season does not produce fruit. [...] Not only [...] comes in this way [...] but also the Sabbath [ⲥⲁⲃⲃⲁⲧⲟⲛ] is barren [ⲁⲧϩⲏⲧ].

**10** Christ came to ransom [ⲛⲁϩⲙ] some, to save [ⲥⲱϩⲉ] others, to redeem [ⲧⲃⲃⲟ] others. He ransomed those who were strangers [ⲡⲁⲣⲉⲡⲓⲇⲏⲙⲟⲥ] and made them his own. And he set apart his own [ⲛⲉⲧⲉⲡⲉϥ ⲛⲉ], those whom he gave as a pledge [ⲁⲣⲣⲁⲃⲱⲛ] according to his will [ⲑⲉⲗⲏⲙⲁ].

**11** It was not only when he appeared [ⲟⲩⲱⲛϩ ⲉⲃⲟⲗ] that he voluntarily [ϣⲁϩⲟⲩⲛ] laid down his soul [ⲯⲩⲭⲏ], but he voluntarily laid down his soul from the very day the world [ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ] came into being. Then he came first to take it, since it had been given as a pledge. It fell into the hands of robbers [ⲥⲟⲛⲉⲧ] and was taken captive, but he saved [ⲛⲁϩⲙ] it. He redeemed the good and the evil in the world.

**12** The light [ⲟⲩⲟⲉⲓⲛ] and the darkness [ⲕⲁⲕⲉ], life [ⲱⲛϩ] and death [ⲙⲟⲩ], the right [ⲟⲩⲛⲁⲙ] and the left [ⲥⲓⲥⲟⲟⲩⲧ] are brothers [ⲥⲛⲏⲩ] of one another. It is not possible for the good to give up the evil [ⲛⲉ ⲁⲛ ϭⲟⲙ ⲛⲧⲡⲉⲑⲁⲛⲉ ⲉⲕⲱ ⲉⲃⲟⲗ ⲛⲡⲕⲁⲕⲟⲛ], nor for the evil to give up the good, nor for life to give up death, nor for death to give up life. For this reason each one will dissolve [ⲃⲱⲗ ⲉⲃⲟⲗ] into its original nature [ⲁⲣⲭⲏ]. But those who are exalted above [ϫⲟⲥⲉ] the world cannot dissolve — they are eternal [ⲁⲓⲱⲛⲓⲟⲥ].

**13** The names [ⲣⲁⲛ] that are given to worldly [ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲓⲕⲟⲥ] things are very deceptive [ⲣⲉϥⲣⲡⲗⲁⲛⲁ], for they turn [ⲉⲡⲓⲥⲧⲣⲉⲫⲉ] the heart [ϩⲏⲧ] from what is real [ⲛⲟⲉⲣⲟⲛ] to what is not real. Thus whoever hears [ⲥⲱⲧⲙ] the word [ⲣⲁⲛ] "God" does not perceive what is real, but perceives what is not real. So also with "the Father" [ⲡⲉⲓⲱⲧ] and "the Son" [ⲡϣⲏⲣⲉ] and "the Holy Spirit" [ⲡⲉⲡⲛⲉⲩⲙⲁ ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲁⲃ] and "life" [ⲱⲛϩ] and "light" [ⲟⲩⲟⲉⲓⲛ] and "resurrection" [ⲁⲛⲁⲥⲧⲁⲥⲓⲥ] and "the Church" [ⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ] — and all the rest. People do not perceive what is real, but they perceive [ⲛⲟⲉⲓ] what is not real, unless they have come to know [ⲉⲓⲙⲉ] what is real. The names that are heard in the world [ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ] deceive. If they were in the aeon [ⲁⲓⲱⲛ], they would not at all times be used as names in the world, nor would they be placed among worldly things. They have an end [ⲧⲉⲗⲟⲥ] in the aeon.

**14** There is one single name [ⲟⲩⲁ ⲛⲣⲁⲛ] that is not uttered [ϫⲟⲟⲥ] in the world — the name that the Father [ⲡⲉⲓⲱⲧ] bestowed upon the Son. This name is above [ⲉϫⲛ] every other name. This is the Father's name [ⲣⲁⲛ ⲙⲡⲉⲓⲱⲧ]: the Son would not have become the Father unless he put on the name of the Father. Those who possess this name know it [ⲥⲟⲟⲩⲛ] but do not speak it [ϣⲁϫⲉ]. Those who do not possess it do not know it.

**15** But truth [ⲧⲙⲉ] brought names [ⲣⲁⲛ] into being in the world for our sakes, because it is not possible to teach [ⲧⲥⲁⲃⲟ] the truth without names. Truth is one [ⲟⲩⲁ]. It is also many [ⲟⲩⲙⲏϣⲉ], and so for our sake she teaches this one thing through many.

**16** The archons [ⲁⲣⲭⲱⲛ] wanted to deceive [ⲣⲉϥⲣⲡⲗⲁⲛⲁ] mankind, since they saw that mankind had kinship [ⲥⲩⲅⲅⲉⲛⲏⲥ] with what is truly good [ⲡⲁⲅⲁⲑⲟⲛ]. They took the names of the good and attached [ⲕⲱ] them to the not-good, so that through the names they might deceive him and bind [ⲙⲟⲣ] him to the not-good. And after this, what a favor they did for them! For they made them leave [ⲕⲱ ⲉⲃⲟⲗ] the free things and take for themselves what is bound [ⲙⲟⲣ].

**17** The farmer [ⲏⲉ] [cannot] do his work without [...] water [ⲙⲟⲟⲩ]. So also, it is impossible to construct [ⲟⲩⲱⲛ] anything without water and fire [...]. The farmer harvests because of water and earth.

**18** God [ⲛⲟⲩⲧⲉ] is a dyer [ⲣⲉϥϣⲱⲙ]. Just as the good dyes — which are called "true" — dissolve [ⲃⲱⲗ ⲉⲃⲟⲗ] together with the things dyed in them, so it is with those whom God has dyed [ⲉⲛⲧⲁϥϣⲱⲙ]. Since his dyes are immortal [ⲁⲧⲙⲟⲩ], they become immortal through his colors [ϫⲣⲟ]. Now God dips those whom he dips in water.

**19** It is not possible for anyone to see [ⲛⲁⲩ] anything of the things that are established [ⲣⲙⲛⲧⲥⲁϩ] unless he becomes like them. It is not the case with mankind in the world [ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ]: he sees [ⲛⲁⲩ] the sun without becoming the sun, and he sees [ⲛⲁⲩ] the heaven and the earth and all other things without becoming them. But in the truth [ⲙⲉ] it is different. You saw [ⲛⲁⲩ] something of that place [ⲙⲁ] and you became [ϣⲱⲡⲉ] those things. You saw the Spirit [ⲡⲛⲉⲩⲙⲁ] — you became spirit [ⲡⲛⲉⲩⲙⲁ]. You saw Christ [ⲭⲣⲓⲥⲧⲟⲥ] — you became Christ. You saw [the Father] — you shall become [the Father]. So in this place [ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ] you see everything and do not see yourself. But there, you see yourself — for you shall become what you see.

**20** Faith [ⲡⲓⲥⲧⲓⲥ] receives; love [ⲁⲅⲁⲡⲏ] gives. No one will be able to receive [ϫⲓ] without faith [ⲡⲓⲥⲧⲓⲥ]. No one will be able to give [ⲧⲁⲁⲥ] without love [ⲁⲅⲁⲡⲏ]. Because of this, in order that we may indeed receive, we believe [ⲡⲓⲥⲧⲉⲩⲉ]. And in order that we may actually give — since if one does not give he has nothing — we love [ⲁⲅⲁⲡⲁ].

**21** Before Christ came [ⲡⲣⲟ ⲛⲧⲉⲭⲣⲓⲥⲧⲟⲥ ⲉⲓ], there was no bread [ⲟⲉⲓⲕ] in the world. As in paradise [ⲡⲁⲣⲁⲇⲉⲓⲥⲟⲥ] — the place where Adam was — there were many trees and food [ⲛⲁⲃⲥⲉ] for the animals, but no wheat [ⲧⲏⲓ] for man. Man used to feed like the animals. But when Christ, the perfect man [ⲧⲉⲗⲉⲓⲟⲥ], came, he brought bread [ⲟⲉⲓⲕ] from heaven in order that mankind might be nourished [ⲧⲣⲉϥⲟⲩⲱⲙ] with human food.

**22** The archons [ⲁⲣⲭⲱⲛ] thought [ⲙⲉⲉⲩⲉ] it was by their own power and will [ⲑⲉⲗⲏⲙⲁ] that they were doing what they did, but the Holy Spirit [ⲡⲉⲡⲛⲉⲩⲙⲁ ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲁⲃ] in secret [ϩⲛ ⲟⲩⲙⲛⲧⲕⲣⲩⲫⲁⲓⲟⲥ] was accomplishing everything through them as it willed [ⲑⲉⲗⲏⲙⲁ].

**23** Truth [ⲙⲉ], which has existed since the beginning [ⲛϣⲟⲣⲡ], is sown [ϫⲟ] everywhere. And many see it being sown, but few are those who see it being reaped.

**24** Some say, "Mary [ⲙⲁⲣⲓⲁ] was impregnated by the Holy Spirit [ⲡⲉⲡⲛⲉⲩⲙⲁ ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲁⲃ]." They are in error [ⲣⲡⲗⲁⲛⲁ]. They do not know what they say. When did a woman [ⲥϩⲓⲙⲉ] ever conceive [ⲱⲟⲡⲉ] by a woman [ⲥϩⲓⲙⲉ]? Mary [ⲙⲁⲣⲓⲁ] is the virgin [ⲡⲁⲣⲑⲉⲛⲟⲥ] whom no power defiled [ⲧⲁⲕⲟ]. She is a great anathema [ⲁⲛⲁⲑⲉⲙⲁ] to the Hebrew apostles and to the apostolic men [ⲁⲡⲟⲥⲧⲟⲗⲓⲕⲟⲥ]. This virgin whom no power [ϭⲟⲙ] defiled [...] the powers defile themselves [ⲧⲁⲕⲟ].

**25** And the Lord [ⲡϫⲟⲉⲓⲥ] would not have said, "My Father who is in heaven [ⲧⲡⲉ]" unless he had another father [ⲉⲓⲱⲧ]. He would simply have said "My Father."

**26** The Lord [ⲡϫⲟⲉⲓⲥ] said to the disciples [ⲙⲁⲑⲏⲧⲏⲥ] [...] "Go into every house and bring what is yours from there. Bring what belongs to the Father's house but do not take nor take away anything."

**27** "Jesus" [ⲓⲏⲥⲟⲩⲥ] is a hidden [ϩⲏⲡ] name; "Christ" [ⲭⲣⲓⲥⲧⲟⲥ] is a revealed [ⲟⲩⲱⲛϩ ⲉⲃⲟⲗ] name. For this reason "Jesus" does not exist in any language, but his name is always [ⲣⲡⲁⲛⲧⲟⲧⲉ] "Jesus" as he is called. "Christ" is also his name in Syriac [ⲥⲩⲣⲓⲁⲕⲟⲥ] and Greek [ⲉⲗⲗⲏⲛⲓⲕⲟⲥ]; in all other languages it is "Messiah" [ⲙⲉⲥⲥⲓⲁⲥ]. "The Nazarene" [ⲛⲁⲍⲱⲣⲁⲓⲟⲥ] is the revealed name of the hidden.

**28** Baptism [ⲃⲁⲡⲧⲓⲥⲙⲁ] is "the holy" and it is the supreme [ⲉϫⲛ ⲟⲩⲟⲛ ⲛⲓⲙ]; redemption [ⲁⲡⲟⲗⲩⲧⲣⲱⲥⲓⲥ] is "the holy of the holy" [ⲡⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲁⲃ ⲛⲛⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲁⲃ]; the bridal chamber [ⲛⲩⲙⲫⲱⲛ] is "the holy of holies" [ⲡⲙⲁ ⲛⲁⲅⲓⲟⲛ ⲛⲁⲅⲓⲱⲛ].

**29** Baptism [ⲃⲁⲡⲧⲓⲥⲙⲁ] includes resurrection [ⲁⲛⲁⲥⲧⲁⲥⲓⲥ] and redemption [ⲁⲡⲟⲗⲩⲧⲣⲱⲥⲓⲥ]; the redemption is in the bridal chamber [ⲛⲩⲙⲫⲱⲛ]. But the bridal chamber is in that which is superior to [...] you will not find [...].

**30** Those who pray [ⲉⲩϣⲗⲏⲗ] for Jerusalem [ϩⲓⲉⲣⲟⲩⲥⲁⲗⲏⲙ] — they love Jerusalem [ϩⲓⲉⲣⲟⲩⲥⲁⲗⲏⲙ]. Jerusalem [ϩⲓⲉⲣⲟⲩⲥⲁⲗⲏⲙ] is the vision [ⲥⲁϫⲉ] of peace [ⲉⲓⲣⲏⲛⲏ]. Jerusalem sees [ⲛⲁⲩ] Jerusalem. The righteous [ⲇⲓⲕⲁⲓⲟⲥ] love Jerusalem.

**31** The holy ones [ⲁⲅⲓⲟⲥ] of holiness [ⲁⲅⲓⲟⲥ] will be nourished [ⲧⲣⲉϥⲟⲩⲱⲙ] by the truth [ⲙⲉ]. [...] There were some who [...] the beasts [...].

**32** In this world those who put on garments [ϩⲃⲥⲱ] are better than the garments [ϩⲃⲥⲱ]. In the kingdom of heaven [ⲙⲛⲧⲣⲣⲟ ⲛⲙⲡⲏⲩⲉ] the garments are better than those who have put them on.

**33** It is through water and fire [ⲕⲱϩⲧ] that the whole place [ⲙⲁ] will be purified [ⲧⲃⲃⲟ] — the visible [ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲛⲁⲩ ⲉⲣⲟϥ] by the visible [ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲛⲁⲩ ⲉⲣⲟϥ], and the hidden [ⲉⲧϩⲏⲡ] by the hidden [ⲉⲧϩⲏⲡ]. There are things hidden through things visible [ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲛⲁⲩ ⲉⲣⲟⲟⲩ]. There is water in water; there is fire in the chrism [ⲭⲣⲓⲥⲙⲁ].

**34** Jesus took them all by stealth [ⲙⲛⲧⲉⲓⲃⲧ]. For he did not reveal [ⲟⲩⲱⲛϩ ⲉⲃⲟⲗ] himself as he truly was [ⲡⲉⲧϥⲟ], but he revealed himself in the manner in which they would be able to see [ⲛⲁⲩ] him. He revealed himself to them all: he revealed himself to the great [ⲛⲓⲟⲥ] as great, he revealed himself to the small [ⲛⲟⲩⲓ] as small, he revealed himself to the angels [ⲁⲅⲅⲉⲗⲟⲥ] as an angel and to men [ⲣⲱⲙⲉ] as a man. Because of this his Logos [ⲗⲟⲅⲟⲥ] was hidden [ϩⲏⲡ] from everyone. Some looked at him and thought [ⲙⲉⲉⲩⲉ] they were seeing themselves. But when he appeared to his disciples [ⲙⲁⲑⲏⲧⲏⲥ] in glory [ⲉⲟⲟⲩ] on the mountain [ⲧⲟⲟⲩ], he was not small. He became great [ⲛⲓⲟⲥ]. But he made the disciples [ⲙⲁⲑⲏⲧⲏⲥ] great so that they would be able to see him in his greatness.

**35** He said on that day in the prayer of thanksgiving [ⲉⲩⲭⲁⲣⲓⲥⲧⲓⲁ]: "You who have joined [ⲕⲟⲓⲛⲱⲛⲓ] the perfect [ⲧⲉⲗⲉⲓⲟⲥ] light [ⲟⲩⲟⲉⲓⲛ] with the Holy Spirit [ⲡⲉⲡⲛⲉⲩⲙⲁ ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲁⲃ], unite [ⲧⲱⲟⲩⲛ] us with the angels [ⲁⲅⲅⲉⲗⲟⲥ] too." Do not despise [ⲡⲁⲣⲁϥⲣⲟⲛⲉⲓ] the lamb [ϩⲓⲉⲓⲃ], for without it it is not possible [ϭⲟⲙ] to see the king [ⲣⲣⲟ].

**36** No one will be able to go into [ⲃⲱⲕ ⲉϩⲟⲩⲛ] the king if he is naked [ⲕⲁⲕ ⲉⲃⲟⲗ]. The one of heaven is clothed if he has put on the light [ⲟⲩⲟⲉⲓⲛ].

**37** Water and fire [ⲕⲱϩⲧ] and light [ⲟⲩⲟⲉⲓⲛ] and the Holy Spirit [ⲡⲉⲡⲛⲉⲩⲙⲁ ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲁⲃ] are the four powers [ϭⲟⲙ]. The perfect [ⲧⲉⲗⲉⲓⲟⲥ] man uses all of them, whether for purification [ⲧⲃⲃⲟ] or for vivification [ⲁⲛⲁⲍⲟⲟⲡⲟⲓⲉⲓ]. The [...] of the bridal chamber [ⲛⲩⲙⲫⲱⲛ] [...] by fire [ⲕⲱϩⲧ] and light.

**38** The Holy Spirit [ⲡⲉⲡⲛⲉⲩⲙⲁ ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲁⲃ] breathes [ⲡⲛⲁ] through everyone [ⲟⲩⲟⲛ ⲛⲓⲙ]. The powers [ϭⲟⲙ] [...] those under the power [ϭⲟⲙ] of [...].

**39** The archons [ⲁⲣⲭⲱⲛ] do not know [ⲥⲟⲟⲩⲛ] where the one who knows [ⲥⲁⲃⲉ] comes from, for he does not want them to know, lest they disturb [ϣⲱⲣϣ] him. Will he not then show them when he is seen?

**40** The cup [ⲡⲟⲧⲏⲣⲓⲟⲛ] of prayer [ⲉⲩⲭⲏ] contains wine [ⲏⲣⲡ] and water [ⲙⲟⲟⲩ]. It serves as a type [ⲧⲩⲡⲟⲥ] of the blood [ⲥⲛⲟϥ] for which they give thanks [ⲉⲩⲭⲁⲣⲓⲥⲧⲉⲓ]. And it is full of the Holy Spirit [ⲡⲉⲡⲛⲉⲩⲙⲁ ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲁⲃ], and it belongs entirely to the perfect [ⲧⲉⲗⲉⲓⲟⲥ] man. When we drink this, we shall receive [ϫⲓ] the perfect man [ⲧⲉⲗⲉⲓⲟⲥ].

**Textual Notes (EMET):**
- *ϩⲉⲃⲣⲁⲓⲟⲥ* / *ⲭⲣⲓⲥⲧⲓⲁⲛⲟⲥ*: The text's opening contrast between Hebrew (ethnic-religious identity) and Christian marks the Valentinian communal self-understanding as a new kind of being, not merely a reformed Judaism.
- *ⲛⲩⲙⲫⲱⲛ* (nymphon): The bridal chamber is the supreme sacrament — a spiritual union that transcends the other four (baptism, chrism, eucharist, redemption). It is not a physical rite but an eschatological state.
- *ⲁⲣⲭⲱⲛ* (archons): Demiurgic powers of the material world, a Valentinian theological concept derived from Platonic cosmology.
- *ⲙⲉ* (me): "Truth" — the Coptic rendering of Greek ἀλήθεια; central theological term throughout.
- *ⲧⲉⲗⲉⲓⲟⲥ* (teleios): "Perfect" in the sense of complete, initiated, spiritually mature — the Valentinian pneumatic.
- *ⲅⲛⲱⲥⲓⲥ* (gnosis): Knowledge of a salvific, direct, experiential kind — distinct from mere intellectual information.
- Lacunae marked [...] reflect actual manuscript damage in Codex II.
- Verses 51/119 and 50/118 show near-duplicate passages within the text, reflecting the anthology's composite nature.
- The Mary Magdalene passage (vv. 51, 119): the lacuna in the manuscript (ⲉⲃⲟⲗ ϩⲛ ⲧⲉⲥ[...]) precedes the body part kissed; "mouth" (ⲧⲁⲡⲣⲟ) appears in some reconstructions but is not preserved in the extant Coptic.
